Ye that obey th' immortal King
Ye that obey th' immortal King,
Bow to the glories of his power,
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 134, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Come, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who serve by night in the house of the LORD! 2Lift up your hands to the sanctuary and bless the LORD! 3May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion. PSALM 134 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 134
Lift up your hands by morning-light, And send your souls on high; Raise your admiring thoughts by night Above the starry sky. STANZA II
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 134. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
